record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.context_brief: Common periodic points for commuting interval maps
record.original_question: If f0 and f1 are commuting continuous self-maps of a compact interval I, must they share a periodic point? Equivalently, is the intersection P(f0) ∩ P(f1) necessarily nonempty, where P(f) denotes the set of periodic points of f?

evidence.quote: Denote by Fix(f) and P(f) the set of fixed and periodic points of a map f ∈ C(I), respectively. We consider two maps f0, f1 ∈ C(I) such that they commute, that is, f0 ◦ f1 = f1 ◦ f0.
Open Problem 5.1. Is it true that P(f0) ∩ P(f1) 6= ∅ for commuting continuous interval maps f0, f1 ∈ C(I)?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $I = [0,1]$ and let $C(I)$ denote the set of continuous self-maps of $I$. For $f \in C(I)$, let $P(f) = \{x \in I : f^n(x) = x \text{ for some integer } n \geq 1\}$ denote the set of periodic points of $f$. Suppose $f_0, f_1 \in C(I)$ commute, i.e., $f_0 \circ f_1 = f_1 \circ f_0$. Must $f_0$ and $f_1$ share a periodic point? Equivalently, is $P(f_0) \cap P(f_1) \neq \emptyset$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether commuting continuous interval maps must share a periodic point appears to remain open. While Boyce and Huneke (1969) showed that commuting continuous interval maps need not share a fixed point, the analogous question for periodic points is still unresolved. Partial results (e.g., Alikhani-Koopaei) show that any counterexample pair must have periodic points of period $2^n$ for every $n$.

status_evidence.title: A Note on Periodic Points and Commuting Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the open problem of common periodic points for commuting continuous interval maps and structural constraints on possible counterexamples.
status_evidence.claim: The common periodic point problem for commuting interval maps is open.

status_evidence.title: On common fixed and periodic points of commuting functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies common periodic points of commuting interval maps; if no common periodic point exists, both maps must have periodic points of period 2^n for all n.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results constrain potential counterexamples but do not resolve the problem.
